title: Admission at the Lift Gate on Lift Tickets
content:
Five limits govern what a Lift Tickets order admits at the lift gate, each of them a term of the product the order was bought on.

| At the gate | The term |
| --- | --- |
| The mountain being scanned at | It must be one the product admits the holder to. |
| A second mountain on a date already scanned | Where the product does not allow more than one mountain on a day, it is refused at the lift. |
| A date on the product's blackout list | It is refused whatever days are left on the order. |
| A date other than the one named on the order | A product that names its ski date admits the holder only on that date. |
| A scan beyond the product's daily limit | It is refused. |

## Two of these limits explained

**The blackout list stands above the days.** A date on the product's blackout list is refused whatever days are left, so days still standing on the order do not carry the holder through such a date.

**The daily limit is not a price.** Scans beyond the product's daily limit are refused as a media protection measure rather than as a charge.

## How the mountain terms read together

A product carries a set of mountains it admits the holder to, and separately carries whether the holder may scan at more than one of them on the same calendar day. Both terms are read at the gate: the mountain has to be within the set, and, on a product that does not allow more than one mountain on a day, the date must not already have been scanned at another mountain.
